To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photocatalytic degradation of the antibiotic gemifloxacin (gemifloxacin, GEM) using titanium dioxide nanoparticles/hydrogen peroxide (TiO2NP/HO2) was successfully optimized using a half-factorial design, and the degradation kinetics of GEM was successfully tracked in-line with a potentiometric ion selective electrode (ISE).
the degradation of gemifloxan (GEM) in aqueous solution using TiO2/H2O2 was optimized and monitored in-line using potentiometric ion selective electrode.
The photodegradation of gemifloxacine (GEM) using titanium dioxide nanoparticles/H2O 2 (TiO 2 NP/H 2 O 2 ) as photocatalyst was investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of a photocatalytic system for the degradation of GEM in water and the in-line monitoring of the degradation process.
the development of a new approach for the degradation of GEM and its photodegradation products in water samples.
the development of a simple, fast, and reliable protocol for the degradation of the antibiotic GEM in water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study is the first report on in-line monitoring of GEM photocatalytic degradation using ISE and the first report on the photocatalytic degradation of GEM using TiO2/H2O2.
the developed method could be used as a promising approach for the elimination of GEM from water samples and its subsequent safe discharge into the environment.
the developed method could be a potential alternative to conventional HPLC methods for monitoring of GEM in the water environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed methodology could provide a new strategy for the treatment of wastewater containing antibiotics and other organic pollutants.
the photocatalytic process was successfully applied for the removal of the GEM and its photodegradation products.
the use of the developed ISE in the optimization process is a promising tool for the in-line monitoring and control of the photocatalytic degradation of GEM in the pharmaceutical industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of TiO2/H2O2 in combination with UV light can be a promising approach for the degradation of pharmaceutical residues, especially in wastewater.
the photocatalytic degradation of GEM is highly effective, and it can be monitored in real time by potentiometric ISE.
in line monitoring of the photodegradation kinetics of gemifloxacine is a promising tool to optimize the photodegradation conditions and ensure the elimination of antibiotic activity.
